meta.ev_method: Two-pass hour-of-day baseline. Pass 1: house baseline for each (date, hour) = 30th percentile of the same hour-of-day over a +/-15 day window. Pass 2: the baseline is recomputed as the median of the same-hour samples with pass-1 EV hours removed. Excess = metered kWh - baseline. Overnight window (8PM-9:59AM): contiguous runs with excess > 2.0 kWh are attributed to the EV provided the run peaks above 4.0 kWh (this keeps the ramp-in/ramp-out hours of a real session while rejecting isolated evening house-load bumps). Daytime window (10AM-7:59PM): only runs of >=2 consecutive hours whose excess is flat (range < 1.0 kWh) and sits between 0.70x and 1.20x the inferred charger power are attributed to the EV; this separates charging plateaus from air-conditioning, which ramps. Per-hour EV is capped at the inferred charger power of 8.02 kW (median of the top decile of overnight excess; consistent with a Tesla Wall Connector at 32 A / 240 V = 7.7 kW). Detected daytime charging = 341 kWh (4.7% of EV energy).
